exact_statement: For n>=3, let F be a Boolean sign with normalized Fourier support minimum Hamming distance at least3, and let Boolean G differ from F at exactly R>=1 vertices. For every relevant ORIGINAL coordinate i, L_i(G)<(37/4)R Inf_i(G). At K=10R the complete-child expected D_K gain is greater than(3/2)R2^-n. Thus a least-essential-dimension positive fixed-K witness, K>=0, has distance R>4K/37 from EVERY such seed; distance0 is also excluded. Linear dependence on the edit count is optimal in order for an ALL-relevant-coordinate guarantee: for every odd k>=3, the explicit Hamming-kernel bent-selector G* on n=r=2^k bits differs from such a seed at r+1 vertices, is tensor-prime with full Fourier support, satisfies H(G*)<=3I(G*), and has L_z/Inf_z>=(r-k-3)(1-1/r), whose ratio to the edit count tends to1. No fresh inherited bank or universal critical-source selection is claimed.
